decisions.reason: Real supply-chain compromise: attacker inserted malicious IPs into Coder's Cloudflare-hosted module registry on Aug 31, exfiltrating credentials via trojanized Terraform modules to coder-infra[.]com. Affects CI/CD and cloud environments.

BigBear 2.0 session hijacking via Evilginx2 rebrand. CloudSEK gained admin access to the panel in June 2026. This is the same campaign as the other BigBear events; assigning to the existing 2-event story.

New RaaS group Panzer: 212 claimed attacks against Italian orgs by early Sept 2026, already exceeding 2025 total. Cross-platform builds, 80/20 affiliate split, automated Bitcoin invoicing. Real operational threat.

Novel electromagnetic side-channel attack: InjectEave recovers audio from consumer headphones at 30m by actively inducing leakage via RF injection. Published at USENIX Security 26. Significant research result.
Detailed follow-on on BigBear 2.0: 42 VPS nodes, 5,137 records from 3,331 IPs across 40+ countries, 1,032 plaintext passwords, 474 MFA bypasses. Same campaign as mf:162823.
Shai-Hulud npm worm reactivated after 111 days with identical payload hash. Four new packages on Sept 7 with preinstall hook that auto-executes. Harvests npm/GitHub/cloud/SSH/CI-CD credentials.
Mathspace breach: 1,079,819 records exposed via unpatched Metabase instance. Access began Aug 10, data exported Aug 27, confirmed Sept 3. Covers students, parents, teachers across Australia/NZ.
Switzerland open-source workplace initiative is government IT policy, not a security event. No vulnerability, breach, or attack.
Bimbo Bakeries USA: SSNs exposed via Oracle E-Business Suite zero-day exploited through third-party vendor. Confirmed Dec 2025, SSNs identified Aug 2026. Real breach with PII.
Same Shai-Hulud npm worm story as mf:162826. Duplicate coverage from GBHackers. Assign to same story.
Duplicate of mf:162824. Switzerland open-source workplace, not a security event.
